title: Separate primary and secondary period fits retain common timing changes in 50 of 207 tested binaries
abstract: We test published ASAS-3 and TESS eclipse measurements without a shared primary and secondary period. Of 304 source-tested binaries, 207 permit four separate linear ephemerides. Fifty have a common epoch or period change at nominal p < 0.001; 20 remain when all fitted errors are doubled. Four also have a differential change. Of 77 source common signals, 25 lack a primary-secondary comparison, 44 meet our coverage rule, and 39 retain a common component. Eleven other systems gain a common detection. Unequal eclipse sampling can mix a pure opposite drift into the source shared-slope estimate. The new fit cancels opposite affine drifts to numerical precision. Tests use real observing designs and 207,000 simulated noise trials. The contribution is a timing test and its population application. These are existing fitted measurements, not new observations. Template correlations, error estimates and selection limit significance. Common timing changes do not alone establish third stars or their population rate.

display.caption: Separate period fits retain common timing changes while a shared slope can mix opposite drifts. Counts use different coverage rules; excluded systems are unresolved.
